title: Fidelity Experiments Sandbox: Developer Kit & Metrics Playbook
author: Maya Ortega
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook describes the Fidelity Experiments Sandbox — a self-service kit for product and engineering teams to run controlled fidelity/latency/cost experiments against Redwood inference surfaces (hosted, dedicated, private). The goal is to make reproducible, auditable experiments that measure end-to-end economics and user-facing fidelity changes before any commercial rollout.

Scope
- Audience: product managers, ML engineers, platform engineers, solutions engineers.
- Environments: staging (primary), canary-hosted (secondary), local-dev (developer preview).
- Not in scope: production billing migrations and any changes to live pricing without separate legal/finance sign-off.

Key concepts
- Fidelity profile: a named set of model/runtime knobs (quantization, sequence budget, prompt-truncation policy, sampling temp) used for experiment runs.
- Fidelity score: a synthetic metric combining quality regressions on prompt sets, hallucination rate, and token-generation divergence (0-100, higher=closer to baseline).
- Economics trace: per-request cost, per-1000-token cost, and aggregate cost for the experiment window.
- Sandbox runner: a reproducible job that replays traffic or synthetic sessions against a fidelity profile and collects telemetry.

Sandbox components and interfaces
1) Sandbox Runner (service: sandbox-runner)
   - Accepts: fidelity_profile id, scenario manifest, input corpus, concurrency, duration.
   - Outputs: fidelity_scorecard.json, telemetry.tar.gz, billing_trace.csv.
2) Developer SDK (package: redwood-experiments-sdk)
   - Python and Go client examples included.
   - CLI: redwood-experiments run --profile <id> --scenario <file> --duration 30m
3) Local Prefetch Proxy (optional)
   - Purpose: enable offline replay with cached embeddings and k-v prefixes so local developers can run realistic end-to-end experiments without touching live model endpoints.
4) Fidelity Decision Service (FDS) (service: fidelity-decision)
   - Simulates production decision logic (route by latency/cost tier, fallback policy) so experiments match runtime routing behavior.

SLOs, metrics and thresholds to collect
- Primary metrics (per-experiment):
  - fidelity_score (target >= 90 for parity experiments)
  - p50/p95 generation latency (ms)
  - per-1k-token cost (USD)
  - regression_count (number of prompts with unacceptable output change)
- Secondary metrics:
  - hallucination_rate
  - average_response_length (tokens)
  - KV cache hit ratio
- Thresholds (example):
  - If fidelity_score < 85 => FAIL
  - If p95 latency increases > 30% over baseline => FLAG for engineering review
  - If per-1k-token cost increases > 20% without fidelity improvement => REVIEW with economics team

Experiment templates (copy-and-run)
1) Baseline parity test (validation)
   Steps:
     1. Create fidelity_profile: baseline (default model + current quantization).
     2. Run sandbox-runner with recorded production sample: 30m, concurrency=10.
     3. Collect fidelity_scorecard and billing_trace.
     4. Confirm baseline fidelity_score >= 95 and store as canonical baseline.
2) Low-cost quantization trial
   Steps:
     1. Define fidelity_profile: quant-4bit-aggressive + prompt-preserve=short.
     2. Run against same input corpus as baseline with sandbox-runner for 60m.
     3. Evaluate fidelity delta, hallucination_rate, and cost delta.
     4. If fidelity_score >= 90 and cost delta >= 18% -> mark candidate for canary.
3) Latency-first routing simulation
   Steps:
     1. Attach FDS with route policy prioritizing p50 < 75ms.
     2. Run mixed traffic scenario (50% short chat, 50% long generation).
     3. Validate routing fallback behavior and per-route economics.

Example experiment manifest (YAML)
---
scenario_name: semantic-search-fidelity-test
fidelity_profile: quant-8bit-conservative
input_corpus: s3://experiments/2026-06/semantic-search-sample.json
concurrency: 25
duration: 45m
metrics: [fidelity_score, p95_latency_ms, cost_per_1k_token, hallucination_rate]
---

Billing & crediting rules (summary table)
| Scenario type | Credit policy | Notes |
|---------------|---------------|-------|
| Development replay | no billing | local proxy; developer credits not consumed |
| Staging sandbox (team) | consumption tracked; credits nominal | uses staging meter; credited to experiment budget |
| Canary public traffic | billed at reduced rate; credits apply | must have finance-approved ticket |

Ownership and roles
- Product owner: Maya Ortega — defines experimental goals, approves pass/fail criteria.
- Platform owner: Liam Chen — maintains sandbox-runner, SDKs, and proxy images.
- ML owner: Priya Kapoor — defines fidelity profiles, evaluation prompt-sets, and gold-answers.
- Finance reviewer: Noah Alvarez — validates crediting and billing outcomes.

Pass/fail and release gating rules
1) Experimental pass if:
   - fidelity_score >= 90 AND
   - p95 latency <= baseline_p95 * 1.15 AND
   - cost change <= +20% unless sponsor approves higher delta.
2) Candidate must pass one canary window (24h with minimum 10k requests) before product rollout.
3) Any safety regression (hallucination uptick > 5% absolute) fails the experiment immediately.

Data capture, privacy and retention
- Telemetry captured: request_id, route, profile_id, latency_ms, token_count, model_variant, fidelity_flags.
- PII policy: experiments may only use anonymized user prompts; recorded corpora must be scrubbed by Solutions or Data Privacy before storage.
- Retention: fidelity_scorecards and telemetry retained for 180 days in experiments S3; longer retention requires compliance approval.

SDK & CLI quickstart
- Install: pip install redwood-experiments-sdk==0.4.0
- Run baseline: redwood-experiments run --profile baseline --scenario ./scenarios/baseline.json --duration 30m --out ./results/
- Generate report: redwood-experiments report ./results/2026-06-10 --format html

Operational runbook (common issues)
- Runner fails to start: check staging IAM role and S3 path access (owner: Platform).
- Divergent baseline: confirm canonical baseline corpus and rerun with identical seed.
- Cost telemetry gaps: ensure billing_trace exporter is enabled in sandbox-runner config (config key: exporters.billing=true).

Rollout checklist for a successful candidate
1. Verify experiment pass and sign-off from ML, Platform, and Product.
2. Run 24h canary in hosted region with production routing (use minimal user-visible cohort).
3. Monitor fidelity_scorecard live; have rollback policy ready in FDS.
4. Open finance ticket for billing migration and credit adjustments.
5. Schedule release notes and customer comms with GTM.

Appendix A — fidelity_score calculation (example)
- fidelity_score = 100 - (10 * normalized_regression_rate) - (5 * normalized_hallucination_rate) - (3 * normalized_divergence)
- Normalization: each sub-metric scaled to 0-1 relative to baseline sample set.

Appendix B — sample JSON result snippet
{
  "experiment_id": "exp-2026-06-10-01",
  "fidelity_score": 92.4,
  "p95_latency_ms": 312,
  "cost_per_1k_token_usd": 0.87
}
